standard_prerequisites.name: Localising the naive cotangent complex

core_obligations: Identify the naive cotangent complex of the given presentation with the explicit two-term complex whose map is the Jacobian matrix, and note that its maximal minors are the displayed polynomials g_I (proof lines 37860-37870).
If some g_I misses the prime, localise at it to get a complex quasi-isomorphic to a free module of rank n - c in degree zero, hence smoothness (proof lines 37872-37878).

Conversely, if all g_I lie in the prime, the complex has no maximal rank after tensoring with the residue field, so no localisation at an element outside the prime can be split injective, hence none is smooth (proof lines 37880-37886).
proof_roadmap: Read the cotangent complex off the presentation and identify the minors (proof lines 37859-37870).
Use a nonvanishing minor, or its absence, to decide smoothness after localisation (proof lines 37872-37887).
difficulty_reason: For a relative global complete intersection S = R[x_1, ..., x_n]/(f_1, ..., f_c) the lemma characterises smoothness at a prime by the existence of a c-element subset of the variables whose Jacobian minor does not vanish at that prime (statement lines 37845-37857). The proof does not compute the differential module directly: it identifies the naive cotangent complex of the presentation with the two-term complex given by the Jacobian, notes that the maximal minors are the displayed polynomials, and then reads smoothness from whether the localized complex becomes a free module of rank n - c, in both directions (proof lines 37859-37887). Relating a nonvanishing minor to the rank of the localized complex is the content. H2.
